title: The rule of 3: what to do first
summary: A simple order of priorities so you don't scatter your efforts when everything stops.
steps: About 3 minutes without air (choking, smoke, drowning): deal with it immediately.
About 3 hours exposed to extreme cold or heat without protection: shelter comes next.
About 3 days without water: secure drinking water third.
About 3 weeks without food: food is almost never the first emergency.
Before all that: get out of immediate danger (fire, collapse, flood, traffic).
tips: These durations are orders of magnitude, not exact limits: they are used to rank priorities.

title: Avoid carbon monoxide poisoning
summary: The leading cause of death during power cuts: generators, braziers and barbecues used indoors.
steps: Never use a generator, barbecue, brazier or fuel-burning heater inside a home, garage or closed tent.
Place a generator outdoors, at least 6 metres (20 ft) from doors and windows.
If a fuel-burning heater is essential, ventilate constantly and never sleep next to it.
Symptoms: headache, nausea, dizziness, drowsiness, often several people (and pets) at the same time.
If in doubt: get everyone into fresh air immediately, then call 112 / 911.
warnings: Carbon monoxide is invisible and odourless: you cannot sense it coming.
Opening a window is not enough to make an indoor barbecue safe.
tips: A battery-powered carbon monoxide detector is an excellent investment for your kit.

title: During and after an earthquake
summary: The right reflexes: drop, cover, hold on, then evacuate carefully.
steps: During the shaking: drop, take cover under a sturdy table and hold on, away from windows.
Outdoors: move away from buildings, trees and power lines; do not run.
After the shaking: turn off gas and electricity if possible, do not light any flame.
Evacuate by the stairs (never the lift) while protecting your head.
Expect aftershocks; do not go back into a damaged building.
warnings: If you smell gas: light nothing, do not use switches, get out and warn others.

title: Facing a flood
summary: Go up, stay out of the water, cut the electricity.
steps: Go upstairs or to high ground with water, food, a light, a radio and your papers.
Turn off electricity and gas if the water is coming, without ever touching a wet appliance.
Never cross a flooded area on foot or by car.
Do not go down into cellars or underground car parks.
Signal your presence to rescuers (white sheet at the window, light at night).
warnings: 30 cm (1 ft) of water is enough to carry a car away; 15 cm (6 in) of moving water can knock an adult over.

title: Fire at home
summary: Get out fast, protect yourself from smoke, close the doors.
steps: If the fire is small and just starting (pan, bin): smother it with a lid or a blanket, cut the gas or electricity. Never put water on burning oil.
Otherwise: evacuate everyone immediately, taking nothing, closing doors behind you.
In smoke: stay low, breathable air is near the floor; cover your nose and mouth with cloth.
Never take the lift.
If the exit is blocked: stay in a room, close the door, seal the gap at the bottom with wet cloths, show yourself at the window and call 112 / 911.
If someone's clothes catch fire: stop them, lay them on the ground and roll them, or wrap them in a (non-synthetic) blanket.
warnings: Smoke kills more than flames: a few breaths can make you pass out.
Before opening a door, touch the handle with the back of your hand: if it is hot, do not open it.

title: Warning siren and sheltering in place
summary: Industrial, chemical or nuclear accident: shut yourself in and listen to the radio.
steps: Recognise the warning siren (in France: rising and falling sound, three cycles of 1 minute 41 seconds separated by 5 seconds; end of alert: continuous 30-second sound). Other countries have their own signals.
Go immediately into the nearest building (not a car).
Close doors and windows, switch off ventilation, air conditioning and forced-air heating.
Seal openings if possible (wet cloths, tape).
Listen to the radio for instructions from the authorities.
Do not go and fetch children from school: teachers shelter them.
Only phone in a life-threatening emergency, to keep networks free for rescuers.
warnings: Only go out at the end of the alert or when ordered by the authorities.
Iodine tablets are taken only on official instructions, and only in a nuclear accident.

title: Storms and high winds
summary: Stay indoors and away from anything that could fall.
steps: Before: bring in or tie down outdoor objects (pots, garden furniture, bins).
Close shutters and windows, charge phones and batteries, prepare lights and a radio.
During: stay indoors, away from windows; avoid travelling.
Never shelter under a tree, and stay away from building sites and the seafront.
After: do not touch fallen power lines, report damage.

title: Heatwave: protect yourself from heat
summary: Especially without electricity or air conditioning: keep your body and home cool.
steps: Drink water regularly without waiting until you are thirsty; avoid alcohol.
Close shutters and windows during the day, open them at night when it is cooler outside.
Wet your body (spray, damp cloth) and fan yourself.
Avoid exertion and going out during the hottest hours; stay in the coolest room.
Check on elderly or isolated people, babies and the sick.
warnings: Never leave a child or an animal in a car, even for a few minutes.
